title: Points, Ticks & P&L
hook: Before you worry about making money, you need to understand how the numbers work.

launchpad.outcome: Calculate a trade's dollar P&L from points, tick value, and contract count, for wins and losses.
launchpad.missionQuestion: If someone tells you they made "50 points today," do you actually know how much money that is?

markers.label: Wins and losses scale the same

slides.headline: Points aren’t dollars.
slides.line: Not until you know the point value and how many contracts you hold.

slides.headline: Point vs tick.
slides.line: Tick size and value differ by contract. Don’t assume every product works like MNQ.

cards.label: Tick
cards.sub: The minimum step. On MNQ: 0.25 points, $0.50.

slides.headline: “I only have a 30-point stop, so I can’t lose that much.”

options.label: Nothing, 30 points is clear
options.feedback: Points alone don’t tell you the dollar risk. You need the point value and contract count too.

options.label: Contract count and point value
options.why: Bingo. 30 points means very different things at 1 contract versus 10.

tool.title: Build your own P&L
tool.body: Points moved × point value × number of contracts. Same chart, same move, different position size, different P&L.

slides.headline: 1 MNQ. Up 10 points.
slides.line: You buy at 20,000. Price rises to 20,010.

options.feedback: That’s just the points. You still need to multiply by the point value.
That’s 10x too much. Check your multiplication.

slides.headline: Short 2 MNQ. Down 15 points.
slides.line: You short at 20,000. Price falls to 19,985, a favorable move.

options.feedback: That’s only 1 contract’s worth. You have 2.
That’s just the points, not multiplied by point value or contracts.

slides.kicker: Not every trade is a winner
slides.headline: 3 MNQ. 10 points against you.
slides.line: The formula doesn’t care about direction. A loss scales exactly like a gain.

options.feedback: That’s only 1 contract’s worth. You have 3.

options.why: 10 points × $2 × 3 contracts = $60 lost, and not every trade is a winner.

options.feedback: Check your multiplication: points × point value × contracts.

slides.headline: 1 point = 4 ticks.
slides.line: Converting between points and ticks works the same way: multiply.

check.prompt: How many ticks are in 2 points?

options.label: 4 ticks
options.feedback: That’s ticks for just 1 point. You need 2 points’ worth.

slides.quote: Points describe price movement. Contracts determine how much exposure you have to that movement.
slides.line: Never discuss risk in points alone without understanding what those points mean in dollars for your position.

slides.prompt: Her friend made 50 points today. Is that a lot of money?
slides.modelAnswer: Points alone don't tell you anything, you need to know the instrument's point value and how many contracts she was holding. 50 points on MNQ with 1 contract is $100. 50 points on MNQ with 10 contracts is $1,000. Same 50 points, completely different amount of money.

takeaways: A point is a whole-number move; a tick is the smallest increment inside it.
P&L = points moved × point value × contract count, for wins and losses alike.
Points alone never tell you the real dollar risk, contracts and point value do.
remember: Never discuss risk in points alone.
